run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-18T02:15:17Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/fraud-detection is defined (rule file otel-demo-otel-demo-alerting-rules, group GoldenSignalAlerts) as sum by (service_name, namespace)(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR", service_name!~"flagd|load-generator"}[2m])) > 0 with for: 1m, so the reported 0.02222 is a per-second rate of ERROR-status spans, not a ratio, and any ERROR span in fraud-detection trips it. The only ERROR-status spans the sampled telemetry attributes to fraud-detection are its CLIENT spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (plus one ResolveInt): in Jaeger each lasts ~594-602 s and ends with otel.status_code ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code 4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), and the paired flagd v0.12.8 server spans for the same traces carry otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" (or gRPC 0). Fraud-detection's actual order work ("orders receive" / "orders process" consumer spans) shows no error tags, and its 10 pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts; no fault-injection flag in flagd-config is enabled (all defaultVariant off). The recorded metric samples for these series stop at 01:45:17 while the alert is stamped 2026-11-18T02:15:17Z, so the exact error spans completing at the alert instant could not be observed and the alert-time value could not be reproduced; in the last sampled minutes the error increase was 0. Whether the ~10-minute stream termination originates in flagd's server-side timeout or in the client-side 600 s deadline of the otel-demo flagd provider remains unresolved, which is why the conclusion is partial and no single root-cause object is asserted.

claims.text: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is defined in Prometheus ConfigMap prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0, key otel-demo-otel-demo-alerting-rules-e2e7e957-0402-4657-b2f5-98974f52e2a1.yaml, group GoldenSignalAlerts: expr sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR", service_name!~"flagd|load-generator"}[2m])) > 0, for: 1m, severity warning, description 'Request error rate in service {{ $labels.service_name }} ... is above 0 (current: {{ $value }})'.

In the sampled span metrics for service_name="fraud-detection" (01:33:17Z-01:44:17Z) the only label sets with status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" are span_kind=SPAN_KIND_CLIENT on span_name flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt; the EventStream error counter stood at 1 for each of the ten exported_instance (pod) values and did not increase (0 increase) in 5-minute and 10-minute windows ending 01:40-01:44.

Jaeger traces for service fraud-detection (version 2.1.3) contain ten client spans on operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR", rpc.grpc.status_code="4" and durations between 594,101,234 us and 601,796,702 us (~600 s); one such trace (bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05) also contains the flagd v0.12.8 server span for the same operation with otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout".

The paired flagd-side spans show mixed results: of 9 flagd EventStream server spans in the error-tagged sample, 2 carry error=true with rpc.grpc.status_code="4" and otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout", while 7 record only rpc.grpc.status_code="0", so the client-side ERROR/deadline outcome is not uniformly reported as an error by flagd.

Fraud-detection's order-processing spans do not show errors: in the 30-trace Jaeger sample (source_start_at 01:34:38Z, source_end_at 01:36:30Z) there are 30 'orders receive' and 30 'orders process' spans, all with status_state=not_recorded and no error details, with orders receive durations between 1,913 us and 98,895 us and orders process durations between 427 us and 927 us.

At query time all ten fraud-detection pods (fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-*) were Running and ready with restartCount 0 and start times 01:19:17Z-01:22:22Z; Deployment fraud-detection has spec.replicas 10, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-fraud-detection and env FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013 with no fault-related environment variables.

The flagd dependency is Deployment flagd in otel-demo (1 replica, container image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8 plus flagd-ui, config mounted from ConfigMap flagd-config into /etc/flagd); Service flagd exposes ports 8013/8016/4000, and pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx was Running with both containers ready and 0 restarts.

ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) defines the otel-demo fault flags adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure, and every one has defaultVariant "off" at query time; none references fraud-detection.

In the last sampled minutes the observed error signal had decayed: the 5-minute error ratio sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="fraud-detection",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]))/sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="fraud-detection"}[5m])) was 0 at 01:38:17Z-01:41:17Z and NaN afterwards, while total fraud-detection span rate fell from 0.4889/s (01:38:17Z) to 0.0324/s (01:41:17Z) and 0 at 01:42:17Z.

The same flagd EventStream pattern is not unique to fraud-detection: service ad also produced ten client spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR", rpc.grpc.status_code="4" and durations 596,886,931-604,202,243 us, with flagd-side spans carrying "stream closed due to server-side timeout".

Other services' error rate in the same sampled window comes from a different failure: checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder ERROR span (rpc.grpc.status_code 13) carries otel.status_description 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to shipping service: Post "http://shipping:8080/get-quote": EOF', with frontend/frontend-proxy 500s on POST /api/checkout in the same trace; the metric error increase for checkout/frontend/frontend-proxy was ~1.08-1.13 per 10 minutes in windows ending 01:40-01:44.

Kubernetes events in the window contain no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Failed events for fraud-detection: the Pod/ReplicaSet/Deployment events are recommendation scale-downs (10 to 8 at 01:35:11Z, 8 to 7 at 01:36:11Z) and data-recorder pod scheduling/PVC provisioning, and the HorizontalPodAutoscaler failures (FailedGetResourceMetric/FailedComputeMetricsReplicas for kafka, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) report 'unable to fetch metrics from resource metrics API (get pods.metrics.k8s.io)' and never name fraud-detection.

The sampled error signal does not show new fraud-detection errors near the end of the available data: the ERROR counters were flat at 1 per pod across 01:33:17Z-01:44:17Z (0 increase in 5m and 10m windows), so the alert's nonzero 2-minute error rate at 02:15:17Z cannot be matched to the sampled series, and the alert instant lies after the newest sample (data_as_of 01:45:17Z, freshness ~2626-2680 s at query time).

Rejected: a feature-flag fault injection aimed at fraud-detection caused the error spans. The flagd-config ConfigMap, which the flagd container mounts at /etc/flagd, has every fault flag at defaultVariant "off" and contains no fraud-detection-specific flag, and the errors are on the flagd EventStream client span rather than on order processing.

Rejected: a fraud-detection pod crash, OOM or restart produced the error spans. All ten fraud-detection pods were Running and ready with restartCount 0 from 01:19-01:22Z, and no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Failed events name fraud-detection.

Most likely mechanism: flagd's EventStream subscription streams are terminated after roughly 9-10 minutes on the server side (flagd span otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout'), and the fraud-detection flagd client records each termination as an ERROR span with rpc.grpc.status_code 4; the 2-minute rate of those completions is what the RequestErrorRate rule sees as 'current: 0.02222', so the alert reflects the flag-stream lifecycle rather than failed order processing.

Alternative and not excluded: the ~600 s duration of every failing span matches a client-side deadline in the otel-demo 2.1.3 flagd provider, and the majority of flagd-side spans end with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, so the DEADLINE_EXCEEDED error may be raised by fraud-detection's own stream deadline rather than by a flagd fault; distinguishing this needs flagd's stream-timeout/keepalive configuration and flagd logs, neither of which is readable here.

gaps: Prometheus samples for traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="fraud-detection"} end at 01:45:17Z (data_as_of) while the alert is stamped 2026-11-18T02:15:17Z; the ERROR spans completing in the alert's 2-minute rate window are therefore not observable, and the specific pod/attempt behind 'current: 0.02222222222222222' is unknown.

No baseline before 01:33:17Z exists for the fraud-detection ERROR series (earliest returned sample), so whether the flagd EventStream deadline errors are new at the incident or long-standing is unknown.

Container logs were empty for fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l (containers wait-for-kafka, fraud-detection) and for flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx (init-config, flagd, flagd-ui): zero lines returned, so no application-level diagnostic of the stream closure is available.

The rule's own evaluation history and pending/firing state could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the alert is known only from the supplied Alertmanager payload and the rule YAML in the Prometheus ConfigMap.

kube-state-metrics series (kube_pod_status_phase, kube_deployment_status_replicas_available, kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason) are not present in this Prometheus (discovery returned no names), so pod availability/readiness was checked only through the live Kubernetes API at query time, not over the incident window.

flagd's stream timeout/keepalive settings are not visible: the flagd container has no args and only FLAGD_*/OTEL_* environment variables, and no flagd ConfigMap key defines a stream timeout, so the value that ends streams at ~550-600 s could not be verified.
change_history is listed as not integrated, so no deployment/configuration change record could be correlated with the alert time.
next_steps: Review flagd v0.12.8 EventStream/keepalive timeout configuration and flagd server logs outside this cluster capture to confirm whether the stream termination is flagd-initiated.

Review the flagd client deadline configuration of the otel-demo 2.1.3 fraud-detection image (~600 s observed) and decide whether long-lived flagd EventStream spans should be excluded (e.g., by span_kind/operation or service filter) from the RequestErrorRate rule, which currently alerts on any STATUS_CODE_ERROR span.

Pull Alertmanager/Prometheus rule evaluation history for 02:13-02:15Z to identify the exact error spans that completed at the alert instant, and check whether RequestErrorRate also fired for ad or other flagd-streaming services at the same time.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888

content:
groups:
- interval: 1m
  name: ClusterAlerts
  rules:
  - alert: FailedPodsDetected
    annotations:
      description: 'Pods in failed state in namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} is above
        0 (current: {{ $value }})'
    expr: sum by(namespace) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="otel-demo", phase="Failed"})
      > 0
    labels:
      severity: critical
  - alert: PendingPodsDetected
    annotations:
      description: 'Pods in pending state in namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} above
        0 (current: {{ $value }})'
    expr: sum by(namespace) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="otel-demo", phase="Pending"})
      > 0
    labels:
      severity: critical
  - alert: CrashLoopBackOffPodsDetected
    annotations:
      description: 'Pods in CrashLoopBackOff state in namespace {{ $labels.namespace
        }} above 0 (current: {{ $value }})'
    expr: sum by (namespace) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{namespace="otel-demo",reason="CrashLoopBackOff"})
      > 0
    labels:
      severity: critical
- interval: 1m
  name: GoldenSignalAlerts
  rules:
  - alert: RequestLatency
    annotations:
      description: 'Latency in service {{ $labels.service_name }} in namespace {{
        $labels.namespace }} is above 1500ms (current: {{ $value }}s)'
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le, service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name!~"flagd|load-generator|accounting|fraud-detection"}[2m])))
      > 1500
    for: 1m
    labels:
      severity: warning
  - alert: RequestLatencyProcessor
    annotations:
      description: 'Latency in service {{ $labels.service_name }} in namespace {{
        $labels.namespace }} is above 15000ms (current: {{ $value }}s)'
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le, service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name=~"accounting|fraud-detection"}[2m])))
      > 15000
    for: 1m
    labels:
      severity: warning
  - alert: RequestErrorRate
    annotations:
      description: 'Request error rate in service {{ $labels.service_name }} in namespace
        {{ $labels.namespace }} is above 0 (current: {{ $value }})'
    expr: sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR",
      service_name!~"flagd|load-generator"}[2m])) > 0
    for: 1m
    labels:
      severity: warning
- interval: 1m
  name: GoodputAlerts
  rules:
  - alert: NoRequestsDetected
    annotations:
      description: Service {{ $labels.service_name }} in namespace {{ $labels.namespace
        }} has 0 requests
    expr: sum by (service_name, namespace) (increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name!~"flagd|load-generator",
      namespace="otel-demo", status_code=~"STATUS_CODE_UNSET|STATUS_CODE_OK"}[2m]))
      == 0
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: warning
- interval: 1m
  name: KafkaAlerts
  rules:
  - alert: KafkaConnectionClosureRate
    annotations:
      description: 'Job {{ $labels.job }} has a closure rate above 0 (current: {{
        $value }})'
    expr: sum by (job) (kafka_consumer_connection_close_rate) > 0
    for: 1m
    labels:
      severity: warning
